name: Vikings
hook: Raiders, traders and settlers from the fjords — and the first Europeans to reach America.

facts.label: the name Viking
facts.statement: "Viking" may come from Viken, a fjord near the future Norwegian capital Oslo, or from an Old Norse word for a bay or fjord dweller.

facts.label: Scandinavia
facts.statement: The Vikings came from Scandinavia; they settled Iceland in 874, and the Althing there, founded in 930, is Europe's oldest parliament.

facts.label: Alfred the Great
facts.statement: Danish Vikings overran England until Alfred the Great of Wessex beat them at Edington in 878; Danegeld was the tax landowners paid to buy them off.

facts.label: Normandy
facts.statement: Around 900 the French king ceded a northern territory to the Viking Rollo, and that duchy became Normandy, home of the Normans.

facts.label: L'Anse aux Meadows
facts.statement: The Vikings reached North America around 1000; L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland is the first authenticated European site there.

facts.label: Erik the Red
facts.statement: Erik the Red founded the first Viking colony on Greenland around 985 and gave the island its inviting name; only 14 of his 25 ships arrived.

facts.label: the 1893 Viking replica
facts.statement: To show Columbus was not first across the Atlantic, a Viking ship replica sailed from Norway to Chicago's 1893 world's fair.
